### Metropolitan Bank Holding Corp. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


October 20, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s206.q4cdn.com/586823346/files/doc_news/Metropolitan-Bank-Holding-Corp--Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf)


***Net Interest Margin Expansion to 4.36%*** ***Diluted EPS of $2.58***


**Financial Highlights**


- Diluted earnings per share was $2.58 for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $1.54 for the prior linked quarter and $0.67 for the prior year period.
- Net interest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $97.6 million, an increase of $7.2 million, or 7.9%, compared to the prior linked quarter and an increase of $20.3 million, or 26.3%, compared to the prior year period.
- The net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 4.36%, an increase of 28 basis points compared to the prior linked quarter and an increase of 48 basis points compared to the prior year period.
- Annualized return on average equity of 13.1% and annualized return on average tangible common equity1 of 13.2% for the third quarter of 2026.
- In support of the Company’s focus on delivering strong shareholder returns, on October 19, 2026, the board of directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.40 per share on the Company’s common stock.
- Total loans at September 30, 2026 were $7.5 billion, an increase of $205.0 million, or 2.8%, from June 30, 2026 and an increase of $723.6 million, or 10.6%, from December 31, 2025.
- Total deposits at September 30, 2026 were $8.3 billion, an increase of $589.1 million, or 7.6%, from June 30, 2026 and an increase of $943.4 million, or 12.8%, from December 31, 2025.
- At September 30, 2026, the Company and Bank displayed strong total risk-based capital ratios of 13.9% and 13.5%, respectively, well above regulatory minimums. The Bank remains “well capitalized” under all applicable regulatory guidelines.


1 Non-GAAP financial measure. See Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures on page 13.


NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Metropolitan Bank Holding Corp. (the “Company”) (NYSE: MCB), the holding company for Metropolitan Commercial Bank (the “Bank”), reported net income of $32.4 million, or $2.58 per diluted common share, for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $19.2 million, or $1.54 per diluted common share, for the second quarter of 2026 and $7.1 million, or $0.67 per diluted common share, for the third quarter of 2025.


Mark DeFazio, President and Chief Executive Officer, commented,


“Our third-quarter performance reflects strong execution across the franchise, with disciplined loan and deposit growth, lower funding costs and continued net interest margin expansion driving meaningful earnings growth. We remain well capitalized, with robust liquidity, and the increase in our quarterly dividend reflects our confidence in the Company’s performance and long-term outlook.”


**Balance Sheet**


Total loans, net of deferred fees and unamortized costs, were $7.5 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $205.0 million, or 2.8%, from June 30, 2026, and an increase of $752.2 million, or 11.1%, from September 30, 2025. The increase in total loans from June 30, 2026 was due primarily to an increase of $164.5 million in commercial real estate (“CRE”) loans (including owner-occupied), an increase of $24.3 million in commercial and industrial (“C&I”) loans and an increase of $19.7 million in construction loans. The increase in total loans from September 30, 2025 was due primarily to an increase of $859.3 million in CRE loans (including owner-occupied), partially offset by a decrease of $97.3 million in C&I loans and a decrease of $8.0 million in construction loans.


Total securities were $1.5 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $399.5 million, or 36.7%, from June 30, 2026, and an increase of $553.5 million, or 59.2%, from September 30, 2025. The increase in securities from June 30, 2026 was due primarily to the deployment of excess cash into short-term securities.


Total deposits were $8.3 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $589.1 million, or 7.6%, from June 30, 2026, and an increase of $1.2 billion, or 17.6%, from September 30, 2025. The increase in deposits from June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025 was primarily driven by the Bank’s EB-5 (Immigrant Investor Program), Home Owners Association banking and retail deposit verticals.


The Bank’s liquidity position remains robust. At September 30, 2026, cash on deposit with the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and available secured funding capacity totaled $4.2 billion, which represented 185% of our estimated uninsured deposits. Total cash and cash equivalents were $247.0 million at September 30, 2026.


The Company and Bank have total risk-based capital ratios well above regulatory minimums. The Bank is “well capitalized” under all applicable regulatory guidelines. Total non-owner-occupied CRE loans were 301.1% of total risk-based capital at September 30, 2026, compared to 304.1% and 376.3% at June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively. The CRE loan concentration ratio declined from September 30, 2025 primarily owing to the increase in the Bank’s total capital as a result of the completion of the Company’s follow-on public equity offering of common stock in the first quarter of 2026.

**Net Interest Income**


Net interest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $97.6 million compared to $90.4 million for the prior linked quarter and $77.3 million for the prior year period. The $7.2 million increase from the prior linked quarter was primarily due to an increase in the average balance of loans and, to a lesser extent, securities, a decrease in the average balance of interest-bearing deposits and a decrease in the total cost of funds, partially offset by a decrease in overnight deposits. The $20.3 million increase from the prior year period was primarily due to an increase in the average balance of loans and overnight deposits and a decrease in the cost of funds, partially offset by an increase in the average balance of interest-bearing deposits.


**Net Interest Margin**


Net interest margin for the third quarter of 2026 was 4.36% compared to 4.08% and 3.88% for the prior linked quarter and prior year period, respectively. The 28 basis point increase from the prior linked quarter and the 48 basis point increase from the prior year period were driven largely by an increase in yields on the average balance of loans and securities, in combination with elevated prepayment penalties and deferred fee recognition as a result of an increased level of loan payoffs, as well as a decrease in the cost of funds.


The total cost of funds for the third quarter of 2026 was 250 basis points compared to 257 basis points and 305 basis points for the prior linked quarter and prior year period, respectively. The decrease from the prior linked quarter primarily reflects improvements in the deposit mix. The decrease from the prior year period primarily reflects the decline in short-term interest rates.


**Non-Interest Income**


Non-interest income was $3.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $392,000 from the prior linked quarter and an increase of $427,000 from the prior year period. The increase from both the prior linked quarter and prior year period was primarily due to an increase in service charges on deposit accounts, partially offset by an increase in the unrealized loss on equity securities.


**Non-Interest Expense**


Non-interest expense was $49.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $2.3 million from the prior linked quarter and an increase of $3.7 million from the prior year period. The $2.3 million decrease from the prior linked quarter was primarily due to a decrease of $1.8 million in other operating expenses, a $1.1 million decrease in professional fees and a $946,000 decrease in technology costs, partially offset by a $1.7 million increase in deposit related program fees.


The $3.7 million increase from the prior year period was due primarily to a $4.1 million increase in compensation and benefits and a $1.8 million increase in deposit related program fees, partially offset by a $1.5 million decrease in technology costs and a $1.1 million decrease in the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”) assessment.


**Income Tax Expense**


The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 29.5% compared to 31.1% for the prior linked quarter and 30.1% for the prior year period. The decline in the effective tax rate reflects the Company's initiation of an investment tax credit purchase program.


**Asset Quality**


The ratio of non-performing loans to total loans was 0.95% at September 30, 2026, compared to 0.91% at June 30, 2026 and 1.20% at September 30, 2025. The slight increase in the non-performing loan ratio from the prior linked quarter was primarily attributable to a single CRE loan being placed on non-accrual status. The decrease from the prior year period reflects the resolution and charge-off of a single CRE loan relationship and a single non-core C&I loan relationship.


The allowance for credit losses was $64.2 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $2.2 million from June 30, 2026, and a decrease of $30.0 million from September 30, 2025. The increase from June 30, 2026 primarily reflects a modest increase in specific reserves and loan growth. The decrease from September 30, 2025 was primarily due to enhancements made to the Bank’s allowance for credit loss estimation process implemented in the first quarter of 2026, as well as the charge-off of the aforementioned previously reserved CRE loan relationship in the second quarter of 2026, partially offset by loan growth.

**About Metropolitan Bank Holding Corp.**


Metropolitan Commercial Bank (“MCB”) is a New York City–based, full-service commercial bank serving businesses, institutions, and individuals who value expertise, responsiveness, and long-term partnerships. Since 1999, MCB has built enduring client relationships, many spanning generations, by delivering consistent, relationship-driven banking.


The Bank provides a full suite of commercial, business, and personal banking solutions, with deep expertise in sectors including real estate, property management, legal services, healthcare, government, and global investors utilizing EB-5 financial solutions. MCB combines specialized capabilities with a highly personalized approach, offering integrated solutions such as title and escrow services, 1031 exchanges, and merchant acquiring.


MCB has received national recognition for its performance and innovation, including being named one of Newsweek’s Best Regional Banks in 2024 and 2025 and earning industry recognition for its lending performance and specialized commercial banking capabilities.


MCB operates full-service banking centers in Manhattan and Boro Park, Brooklyn, within New York City; Great Neck on Long Island; Lakewood, New Jersey; and in South Florida, including Miami, and West Palm Beach.


Metropolitan Commercial Bank is a New York State–chartered commercial bank, a member of the Federal Reserve System and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, and an equal housing lender. The Bank’s parent company is Metropolitan Bank Holding Corp. (NYSE: MCB).


For more information, please visit the Bank’s website at[MCBankNY.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.mcbankny.com%2F&esheet=54625549&newsitemid=20261020304608&lan=en-US&anchor=MCBankNY.com&index=4&md5=352293dea4f36f177fa3c720cba9a92e) .
